title: Rendering
body: One universal renderer produces a page per visible document at the path of its source: `docs/src/a/b.json` becomes `docs/out/a/b.md`. Pages start with a comment saying they are generated. ^35ps

The title is the first level heading. Under it comes one line with the kind, status, priority and tags separated by a middle dot, then the body without a heading of its own, then the free fields in file order, each as a second level section named after the field. At the end of the page come the sections Parent, Referenced by (documents that point here through `parent` or through references outside `notes`) and Covered by (the paths of code files with a `docc:` tag, without line numbers). There is no separate section of links: the references stay in the text. ^vew8

A reference to a document becomes a relative link whose text is the title of the target; a reference to a field or to a section inside a field links to its heading. A field made of sections is a second level heading with third level headings (up to the sixth) for the sections; in the single HTML file they appear in the table of contents of the page. Objects become bullet lists and arrays of objects become numbered lists; when every object has the same plain fields in the same order they become a table. Empty values create no section. ^9v95

The file `docs/out/_tree.md` shows the documents nested by parent, starting with the roots; with `"tree": "folders"` it shows the folders instead ([[config@5wdq]]), and so does the tree of the HTML file, a folder without a page of its own as a line with its name that folds, and a folder with a title-only page ([[config@5wdq]]) as such a line with that title. Pages with the same parent, and the pages without a parent, are sorted by `order`, and the pages without it come after the rest, sorted by title: ignoring case, numbers by value, Latin before Cyrillic, with the same rules on every machine; equal titles go by id. ^mzp5

With `"numbering": true` in `docc.json` docc numbers the pages: the children of the roots get 1, 2 and so on, deeper pages 2.1, and the sections of a field 2.1.1. The numbers appear in headings, in the tree, in the navigation and in the text of links; anchors do not change. Hidden documents are left out of the count, so the audit build shows the same numbers. A number typed into a title or a section key is reported as DOC314. ^m8n3
`"lang": "ru"` in `docc.json` translates the fixed labels of the pages and of the single HTML file, such as Parent, Referenced by and Covered by; the default is English. ^jvez

An image `![alt](path)` with a relative path is resolved from the folder of the document, checked by DOC213 and copied into the output folder at the same path as in the sources; the single HTML file and `docc compile` embed it as a data URI. An SVG data URI is kept only as the source of a picture: in a link it is emptied like `javascript:`, since a browser runs the scripts of an SVG opened as a page but not of a picture. Markdown footnotes are rendered in the HTML file. A fenced `mermaid` code block stays code in the Markdown and in `docc compile` (a program that shows the pages draws it itself); the single HTML file draws it offline with mermaid 12.2.0, embedded (about 5.5 MB) only when a page has such a block, with `securityLevel` strict and the light or dark theme of the page; a syntax error keeps the source and shows the error under it. ^bh67

The flags single and html of docc build also write all pages into one file next to the folder: docs/out.md and docs/out.html. The pages follow the order of the tree, and links between them are anchors inside the file, so the file works on its own. The Markdown file starts with the tree and puts an invisible anchor before every page and field section. ^ac5n

The HTML file is a single-page application that needs no network: Preact with htm (about 13 kB, embedded, no build step), the styles and a JSON island with the pages are inside. It suits any documentation (technical, internal, for a customer, a book), so it says nothing about who reads it. docc renders the Markdown of every block to HTML; the script draws one page at a time in a single mode: the header (the project name, the timeline button, on narrow screens the menu and the search, and ⋯ with Reset everything), the left column with a search box and the tabs Pages and Comments, and the page with its breadcrumb trail, one-line fields collected into a property list, its child pages with the start of their text and the neighbours in tree order. Search finds paragraphs, says how many, and opens the page at the paragraph; the keys / and Ctrl+K open it. The address `#<id>/<JSON Pointer>` opens a page at a paragraph, an unknown address says that nothing is found there, and Back returns to the place of reading. In the tree, titles of pages of one level line up behind an icon of the document kind (a plain file for a kind without its own icon) and the fold arrow sits on the right; the headings of the open page, each marked #, share one card with it. The top level of the tree is always open and has no fold arrow; below it the tree starts folded and opens only the way to the current page, documents without a parent follow the tree at its top level, and long lists show a window of items with buttons for the rest, so a thousand documents stay usable. Like the file status of an IDE, the tree shows the edits between the two ends of the timeline: the title of a page with edits is blue with their number beside it, a page created in that period is green with a plus, and a folded page with such pages below it has a dot; deleted documents have no history, so they are not in the tree. The kind, status, priority and tags of a page and its related pages are not shown in the HTML file (the Markdown has them); in the full build a hidden page is marked hidden. The left column is docked from 1280 px and slides in as a modal panel on narrower screens; on a touch screen and below 820 px every control is at least 44 px. Reset everything deletes, after a question, all the file keeps in the browser: the name, the timeline, the open tab and the comments. The theme follows the system; print gives the current page. Without scripts the file shows a note. Raw HTML written in the documents is dropped, only the line break in table cells is kept. The look is fixed, there are no templates; the only change is the branding below. ^9jyx

A block is one element of a document: a string of an array of strings, or the whole value of another field or section (a table or a list is one block). It is addressed by the document id and the JSON Pointer of the element, such as `/body/2`. The history of every block is read from Git at build time: every version that changed its text; the uncommitted state of the working tree is the last version. Inserting a paragraph does not move the history of its neighbours: the strings of an array are matched by equal text, then by similar text, and the pairs keep their order, so a paragraph removed in one place and one added in another stay a removal and an addition. People outside the team may read the file, so the default build leaves out the hidden fields (notes, docIgnore, hidden), the versions in which a document was hidden (a page written hidden starts its history when it is shown, one hidden for a while goes on from the last version shown), the authors and messages of the commits and, with `docc build --html --since <revision>` (a Git revision to show the edits from, such as the version a reader last saw), everything before that revision; the full build keeps it all. The timeline sits behind a button in the header that sums it up (Edits: 11 days ago → now; a moment in the past by its exact time); it opens under the header on a wide screen and as a sheet from the bottom on a narrow one, so the header keeps its height. It puts the saved versions on one track with two ends, Edits since and Text as of, each with its relative and exact time; the points are evenly spaced, because saves come in bursts, and those that changed the page are darker (with more than 120 saves only those get a point). Below the track a date field shows the text as of the last save of that day, and a box keeps only the saves that changed the page (on from 120 saves). The saves follow by day, newest first: a day is one line with its number of saves and of those of this page, the day of Text as of and the newest are open, and days and the saves of a day come 15 at a time. A save shows the exact and relative time and a mark if it changed the page; picking one shows what it changed (the edits from the save before it, the text at it), as in the version history of Google Docs, and on the picked save a button shows the edits after it up to now. Below 820 px the sheet closes after a pick or a date and has a Close button, and its top stays put while the list scrolls; on a touch screen with more than 120 saves there is no track, since a finger cannot pick one of thousands of saves on it, so the days and the date do. The timeline drags the thumbs itself (the range inputs stay for the keyboard): a press by mouse or finger takes the nearer thumb, a press on the bare track moves it there, and of two thumbs closer than a thumb (as after a pick) the first move decides: to the left Edits since, to the right Text as of. A long list is drawn only while the timeline is open. Edits since starts at `changesSince` (else at now, which shows no edits) and is kept in the browser; Text as of opens at now. With Text as of in the past the page shows its text at that moment, like the version history of Google Docs: the build adds the rendered HTML of the old versions of string blocks (old tables, lists and objects show as plain text), blocks that came later are left out, blocks removed later are back in place, and a note says which moment is shown, with a button back to now; comments are left on the current text only. The edits between the two ends are drawn in the text like a Git or IDE diff: the words of the old version are matched with the words of the rendered paragraph, so links, lists and tables stay, added words are underlined on green and removed ones struck out on red; a rewrite (under 40% shared words) and a code block show the previous text folded above instead. A bar left of a paragraph marks it changed (blue) or added (green, with a plus); a removed paragraph stays folded at its old place. The tree shows where the text changed, and the list shows what changed on the open page: over the tree the button Edits on the page with their number (on a page without edits it says so and is inactive) opens the list beside the tree (on a narrow screen in its place in the panel, with a button back to the pages); it stays open across pages, follows the open page and closes with its button or Close. On top it shows the page, its labelled counts and the period; the rows stand under the headings of the page, every row is marked edited, added or removed with the start of its text on one line and opens the paragraph, and 15 rows come at a time. A button below opens the next page with edits in the order of the pages (after the last one the first) at its first edit, so all the edits can be gone through without the tree. Outside a Git repository there is no history and no timeline. ^7rwz

A comment is left on selected words: a selection shows the button Comment on the selection (on a touch screen in the bottom bar); paragraphs have no buttons of their own. It is a card on the right margin that does not make its paragraph taller (under the paragraph on a narrow screen); the margin opens only on a page with comments or an open editor. The fragment is highlighted and kept with a few characters around it, and a card whose fragment is gone says so. A browser comment from an older build whose words left its paragraph (a paragraph was inserted above) shows on the nearest paragraph that has them. The comments of the documents (`$comments`) stand on their blocks; those that lost their place are listed at the top of the page, and an answer stands at its form field wherever the field went. A comment made in the browser gets an id like those of `docc comments apply`. On a touch screen Edit, Delete and Undo are 44 px tall, the bottom bar hides while the editor has focus, the text box grows to 40% of the screen with Save in sight under it, and the page shrinks for the on-screen keyboard where the browser allows it. A comment is typed or dictated: the button Dictate turns on the speech recognition of the browser and it records until the button is pressed again, starting again by itself after a pause (Chrome and Edge send the sound to their speech service). The first visit asks for the reader's name in a small dialog (Skip leaves it empty, and then the editor asks for it first); it fills the field From of every comment, ⋯ shows and changes it, and Reset everything asks again. The field From can still be changed, so a call can record comments of more than one person; a comment can be edited, and its deletion undone. Comments stay in the browser until they are imported into the documents; the tab Comments is a flat list of the browser's and the documents' comments (one without a place is marked page removed or paragraph removed), and it copies them as text for a messenger, ending with a `docc-comments:` line for the import, or downloads them as a JSON file; `docc comments import` takes either ([[commands@nmzt]]). Comments of the documents appear on their blocks and in the tab; a browser comment that is already there leaves the browser. The Markdown pages show a comment under its block as a quote, the author, the date, the selected words and the text, an answer to a form field where the field would stand, and the lost ones at the top of the page. A comment in the tab opens its page at its paragraph with its card, unfolded among the others; an accepted comment often outlives its place (the answered question is deleted), so one whose page or paragraph is gone is marked page removed or paragraph removed and opens in the list with the words it was left on, and with a link to the page when only the paragraph is gone. The card of a comment from the documents that has `edited` shows edited and the date of the edit beside its date. The cards stand beside the text when the page has room for them, also with the list of edits open, and under their paragraph otherwise. ^d9wj

A form field of the sources (see [[document-model#form_fields@m7sb]]) is drawn in its place: the question, the choices as radio buttons or check boxes, or a text box, and Save; radio buttons and check boxes end with Own answer and a text box (radio: instead of the options, check boxes: besides them), which shows an own answer given before; a reader without a saved name gets a From box too. The answer is kept in the browser as a comment with the id of the field, the value given, the same in words and the field as it read; one browser keeps one answer per field, a later one takes the place of the earlier one. Answers have no cards: under the field the list Answers shows the latest answer of each author, marked to an earlier question when the question or its choices changed after it, and the reader's own one with in this browser and Delete. Answers leave the page with the comments; a file with answers is version 2, so an older docc refuses it rather than drop them. An imported answer is written next to its field, found by id; in the document it keeps the field id and the value given, not the words. In the past of the timeline the fields are disabled, and a changed field shows its old text. A selection inside a field opens no comment. ^zy4c

The `branding` section of `docc.json` dresses the HTML file for a company: `name` (required), `url`, `logo` (a path from the project root; png, jpg, jpeg, gif, svg or webp, embedded once in the file), `accent` (dark theme and header), `accentLight` (links on the light theme; it must read on white) and `header` (background of the header, default #1f1f1f). The logo and the name sit on a dark header at the top of the sidebar and in the mobile bar, so a light logo is expected. A footer at the end of every page shows the name and the site. On paper the header turns into the name above a line in the accent colour; no background is printed. Without the section the file does not change, and the Markdown output is never branded. The year is not in the footer, so the file does not go stale on the first of January. A missing or wrong logo, a colour that is not `#rgb` or `#rrggbb` and an unknown key are configuration errors (exit code 2). ^z3yy

The output is deterministic: stable sorting, no timestamps, line feeds only, UTF-8 without a byte order mark. Carriage returns and byte order marks in input files and in the output folder are normalized when reading and comparing. ^ejxc
audit_build: The flag full on build adds hidden documents, notes and suppressions as service sections, and wraps every include in comments that show where the inserted text starts and ends. ^gj35
